{"local_delta": 0.03,
  "departures": [
    {"fact": "Division is the country's first 'sanctuary' for transgender youth care, and its statute shields families — including families who travel here — from child-abuse investigation or prosecution for seeking gender-affirming care.",
     "local_evidence": "\"In September 2022 the governor signed a state bill making this state/province the first to declare itself a sanctuary for transgender young people seeking medical care... the law shields families from child-abuse investigations or criminal prosecution for seeking gender-affirming care, including families who travel to the state/province for it.\"",
     "direction": "safer",
     "magnitude": 0.04,
     "visitor_applicability": "Directly traveller-facing for visiting families/young people seeking care here, and a documented protective institutional posture; does not touch federal border/passport exposure.",
     "already_in_national_bundle": false,
     "counted_in_delta": true},
    {"fact": "Division's own corrections system documents identity-based housing within the general population and state-funded gender-affirming surgery for transgender inmates.",
     "local_evidence": "\"As of January 2021 this state/province is coded as the single sub-unit allowing transgender inmates to be housed according to their gender identity... In 2015 this state/province became the first sub-unit to fund gender-affirming surgeries for transgender prison inmates.\"",
     "direction": "safer",
     "magnitude": 0.02,
     "visitor_applicability": "Only reaches a visitor if taken into the division's custody; the placement rule is the tier-1 analogue (custody placement), the surgery funding is largely resident-facing. Last documented January 2021, so weight kept small.",
     "already_in_national_bundle": false,
     "counted_in_delta": true},
    {"fact": "Division recorded the highest raw count of anti-LGBTQ incidents of any sub-unit in 2025 (198 of >1,000 nationally).",
     "local_evidence": "\"A national LGBTQ monitoring group documented more than 1,000 anti-LGBTQ incidents nationwide in 2025, of which this state/province recorded 198, the highest figure of any state/province. That ranking is by raw count only: the source supplies no population or per-capita denominator.\"",
     "direction": "riskier",
     "magnitude": 0.01,
     "visitor_applicability": "LGBT-wide, not trans-specific; without a denominator the bundle itself says it does not establish higher per-visitor risk. Given minimal weight, not zero.",
     "already_in_national_bundle": false,
     "counted_in_delta": true},
    {"fact": "Law-enforcement data show a 'dramatic increase' in anti-LGBTQ hate-crime reports in the division's largest city, in the same period as the governor's platforming of anti-trans figures.",
     "local_evidence": "\"A separate analysis of the same 2025 incident data reports a dramatic increase in anti-LGBTQ hate-crime reports in the state/province's largest city in law-enforcement data covering the same period as the governor's platforming of anti-trans figures.\"",
     "direction": "riskier",
     "magnitude": 0.02,
     "visitor_applicability": "Local social-hostility signal in the city a visitor is most likely to enter; report-count trend, LGBT-wide, no per-capita rate, so weighted modestly.",
     "already_in_national_bundle": false,
     "counted_in_delta": true},
    {"fact": "Division sits in a top-tier 'safest laws' band (4.1 protective-law score) in a July 2026 analysis.",
     "local_evidence": "\"A July 2026 analysis places this state/province in a top-tier protective-law band with a score of 4.1 and 1.9 recorded incidents.\"",
     "direction": "safer",
     "magnitude": 0.02,
     "visitor_applicability": "Largely resident-facing statutory stock and an unstated methodology (what '1.9 incidents' counts is not defined); treated as climate signal overlapping the sanctuary statute, so not separately counted.",
     "already_in_national_bundle": false,
     "counted_in_delta": false}
  ],
  "inherited_national_exposure": [
    "Federal document regime: January 2025 executive order defining sex as binary at conception, passport/visa self-selection barred, foreign ministry halting X markers and non-matching markers (Feb 2025), Supreme Court permitting it (Nov 2025), passports confiscated/blocked, litigation pending.",
    "Border screening: Feb 2025 visa flagging and permanent fraud-based ban for applicants listing a gender other than assigned sex; trans-athlete entry ban; allied governments' travel advisories.",
    "Federal facility/funding measures: orders barring federal funding of single-sex facilities congruent with identity, rescinding prison LGBTQ policies, care-related funding freeze and health-rule proposals (in force or enjoined).",
    "Federal custody exposure: corrections bureau policies (from 2026) mandating hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; unreported transgender prisoner counts; immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse.",
    "State/province-level variance already priced in nationally: bathroom bans in 9 sub-units plus one, criminal bathroom use in some, marker-change maps, a Feb 2026 sub-unit law voiding mismatched documents, and 4 sub-units flagged 'Do Not Travel'.",
    "Nationally documented hostility and partial recourse: 2025 polling on documents/athletics, 27 sub-units banning youth care, national gender-identity hate-crime statute but thin state-level bias-crime coverage (23 of ~60), anti-activist bounty instruction and counterterrorism language."
  ],
  "uncertainty": "Whether the January 2021 identity-based custody practice persists is unconfirmed (no later source either way). No local data on facilities/bathrooms, ID-marker rules, entry screening or hate-crime statute coverage — the bundle states those layers sit in the national record or are uncovered, so no local credit is taken for their absence. The 4.1/1.9 July 2026 figures have unexplained methodology; the 198-incident count and the city hate-crime rise have no per-capita denominator, so both are weak and were weighted accordingly. Whether the city increase reflects incidence or reporting is unresolved.",
  "notes": "Net +0.03: two documented local protective departures (the travelling-family sanctuary statute, and identity-based custody placement with funded inmate care, the latter dated to January 2021) against two weak, non-trans-specific local hostility signals. The sanctuary statute is the only clearly traveller-facing positive; the raw-count and city-report items were deliberately kept small per the no-denominator rule and the bundle's own caveat. No local departure removes the inherited federal border, passport and custody exposure, so the division stays close to, not far above, the national line."
}
